forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor, IMF PortWatch, UNCTAD Maritime Trade, or Lloyd's List reports ≥50 daily transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window.

If ≥2 independent sources cannot confirm independence within the resolution window, default to AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Western insurer coverage refusal is a sufficient condition for AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO regardless of reported transit counts.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's governing coalition lose its 61-seat Knesset majority (via defection, dissolution motion, or no-confidence) before the mandatory 2026-10-27 election date?
forecasts.delta_reason: Major structural shift since May 19. Dissolution bill filed by coalition whip Ofir Katz (~May 19-20); passed preliminary Knesset reading 110-0 on May 20, with co-sponsorship from UTJ (Degel HaTorah + Agudat Yisrael), Shas, Religious Zionist Party, and Otzma Yehudit — every significant coalition faction. The actual coalition seat count is reported at approximately 60 as of May 2026, one below the 61-seat governing threshold, per multiple sourced Israeli political reports. Channel 12 poll (May 29) projects coalition at only 51 seats at a hypothetical election. First formal reading of the dissolution bill scheduled June 1. Netanyahu has publicly targeted October as his preferred election month; Assaf Shapira (Israel Democracy Institute) assesses September-October as most likely range. Cold-start audit (Sunday): gap inherited 0.35 vs cold ~0.78 confirmed (43pp). Judge selects 0.75 — close to cold-start, with 3pp reduction to account for procedural risk (Netanyahu retains tools to slow second reading) and the distinction between coalition operationally below 61 vs confirmed Knesset roll-call vote record. Verb correction applied: 'publicly indicated' (not 'signalled') used throughout.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu formally announces an early election date that moves the election earlier than 2026-10-27 (formal Knesset speech or published government decision required). NO if coalition survives to the mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact throughout.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record plus Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel confirmation. Polling alone does not resolve. Reviewed weekly on Sundays only; no intra-week deltas allowed per Codex DA #12.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: counts as YES (majority lost). If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: counts as NO. VOLUNTARY DISSOLUTION ADDENDUM (Judge, 2026-05-31): A government-initiated dissolution bill passing all formal Knesset plenum readings by a majority vote also counts as YES for this forecast, because formal dissolution by definition moves the election date earlier than the Oct 27 mandatory date. The question of who initiated dissolution (opposition vs government) is irrelevant; what matters is whether the coalition majority of 61+ is formally confirmed lost via official Knesset record.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US confirm a signed written framework agreement (containing both a Hormuz/ceasefire element AND an explicit nuclear negotiation framework component) before EOD 2026-06-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: Diplomatic progress since May 19 is real but has not cleared the resolution threshold under strict principal-confirmation criteria. Key sequence: May 23 — Trump described deal as 'largely negotiated' (CNN); May 24 — both sides walked back expectations of imminent breakthrough; May 28 — Axios and Al Jazeera reported tentative 60-day truce MOU reached at envoy level, contingent on Trump's final approval; May 29 — Trump held Situation Room meeting without final determination; May 31 — Axios reports Trump sent edits back to Iranian side targeting nuclear enrichment specifics and Hormuz wording, with US officials projecting approximately 3 days for Iranian response. As of May 31 EOD: MOU text is approximately 80% agreed but NOT signed. Edit-response-loop timeline (Iranian response ~June 3, Trump review ~June 4-5 best case, dual principal public confirmation within 72h) makes EOD June 5 structurally constrained. Strict ambiguity_rule requires principal confirmation (Trump + Pezeshkian or his office), not envoy-level agreement alone. VP Vance confirmation does not suffice. Cold-start audit: gap inherited 0.25 vs cold ~0.10 (15pp). Judge selects 0.13 — above cold-start floor (parties are genuinely in final stage with 80% agreed text) but well below 0.52-0.58 DA recommendation (REJECTED: conflates deal-happening-generally with deal-happening-before-June-5-under-strict-principal-criteria). N1 (June 7 horizon, p=0.35) captures the more probable near-term signing window.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official (Trump personally, or Secretary Rubio citing Trump's explicit written public authority) AND a named Iranian official (President Pezeshkian or his office, OR FM Araghchi with explicit Pezeshkian office endorsement within 72h) both publicly confirm a signed written framework containing both (a) a Hormuz/ceasefire element AND (b) an explicit nuclear negotiation framework component. Text authenticated by both sides or published by Axios/Reuters/State Dept/Iran MFA with dual acknowledgment counts. A standalone ceasefire extension MOU without a named nuclear negotiation framework component does NOT constitute YES. Verbal 'agreement in principle' without document text or dual authentication does not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At minimum Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP quoting named US AND Iranian principals (not envoys alone). Official Iranian Foreign Ministry statement or US State Dept press release also resolves if dual-confirmed. Social media posts by Trump alone count only if Iran's side (Pezeshkian or his office) confirms within 24h.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreement by envoys only, without principal confirmation (Trump/Pezeshkian) within 72h of announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran FM Araghchi confirms but Khamenei's office disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. VP Vance confirmation alone, without Trump's explicit public authority delegation, does NOT trigger YES. Araghchi counts as Iranian principal ONLY IF Pezeshkian's office explicitly endorses his statement within 72h. A ceasefire MOU without nuclear framework component = NOT YES. 'Agreement in principle' phrasing without document text = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.
